dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Rather than eat up these predictions on futures from the experts at the Exchange, I might as well get myself a lucrative dish.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Exchange...

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Oh, the Kalimi Exchange. It's a place where you can see people's strengths, courage, and insights in action.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: If you have the assets and the wealth, as well as sound judgment, you can really turn a profit here.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Sufficient wealth isn't a problem for a bona fide noble like myself. The Homayanis haven't got anything on my family!

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: No, all I'm missing right now is an opportunity... to make my family fortune even more abundant. That way, my children can rest easy knowing that they won't have to go be merchants!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Good grief, not a single one of these amateurs is reliable!

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Everything is smoother with money!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you are...

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: I'm the descendant of the oldest aristocratic family in the desert, which is basically synonymous with wealth itself.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: It's too bad. Researchers who are not from Vahu{RUBY#[S]Aetiology}mana would never understand the value of this status. City folk these days...

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: It's not merely a problem about Mora, but also wisdom and courage.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Whether it's Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's legacy or King Deshret's relics, all can be found in my family's treasury.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: The estate left to me by my ancestors will continue to flourish in my hands.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are...

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: I'm the descendant of the oldest clan of desert aristocrats. Our name is synonymous with wealth itself.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: It's just a huge shame that researchers who are not from Vahu{RUBY#[S]Aetiology}mana will never understand the value of that status. City folk these days...

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: But it's not merely a problem about Mora, but also wisdom and courage.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Whether it's the Dendro Archon's legacy or King Deshret's relics, all can be found in my family's treasury.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: The estate left to me by my ancestors will continue to flourish in my hands.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You might go broke.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Oh relax! With my considerable wealth, I'm sure I won't easily go broke.

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: Even if it's just half of my wealth, it's still three times the worth of the Kalimi Exchange!

dialogues.speaker: Hatim
dialogues.text: See this antique? Ten a penny in my house. Take it if you want it!
